content.title: NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament Championship Live Updates: Michigan Wins National Title
content.text: Apr 06, 2026 - 7:55p ET Live Scoreboard Live Coverage for this has ended Apr 06, 2026 - 11:52p ET Post-game Celebrations Yaxel Lendeborg fought through a knee injury to play a team-high 36 minutes and score 13 points. He celebrated that effort after Michigan's win.Aday Mara didn't really need the ladder, but he used it anyways to cut down the nets after Michigan's title victory.Apr 06, 2026 - 11:15p ET UConn's Final Push The UConn Huskies turned up the heat with a full-court press, leading to a Michigan turnover and Solo Ball 3-point shot to cut the margin to four. Apr 06, 2026 - 11:06p ET The Freshman Comes Up Big Michigan freshman Trey McKenney hit a right-wing 3-point shot to put the Wolverines up nine points with 1:49 remaining. McKenney's triple came after UConn failed to convert a transition opportunity — a 5-point swing that could determine the outcome.Apr 06, 2026 - 10:44p ET UConn Sticking Close To Michigan Down the Stretch Michigan took an 11-point lead, but UConn isn't going away. Alex Karaban went coast-to-coast and Silas Demary Jr. got on the board to cut the margin to five. Apr 06, 2026 - 10:29p ET Michigan Extends Lead to Double Digits Elliot Cadeau hit a 3-point shot from the top of the key to extend Michigan's lead to 48-37. Cadeau drove for a right-handed layup on the possession prior and is leading the Wolverines in scoring with 15 points. Apr 06, 2026 - 9:50p ET Roddy Gayle Jr.'s Dunk Powers Michigan Surge Roddy Gayle Jr. followed up Yaxel Lendeborg's missed transition layup with a perfectly-timed putback dunk. The Wolverines ended the half on an 8-4 run to take a 33-29 lead into the break. Apr 06, 2026 - 9:42p ET Michigan Back In Control The Wolverines retook a four-point lead after layups from Aday Mara and Yaxel Lendeborg. UConn had controlled the tempo with its physicality and energy, but Michigan is building momentum. Apr 06, 2026 - 9:22p ET UConn Goes Ahead Alex Karaban hit a 3-point shot to give UConn a 16-13 lead, then Malachi Smith's layup added to it. The Huskies are up 18-17 at the under-eight timeout. Their defense boosted them into the lead as they held Michigan to 37% from the field through the first 12 minutes. Apr 06, 2026 - 9:11p ET Michigan Takes An Early Lead The No. 1 seed Wolverines jumped out to an 11-10 lead. Point guard Elliot Cadeau had seven of their first 11 points. Forward Solo Ball hit two 3-point shots to keep the Huskies close. Apr 06, 2026 - 8:12p ET Injury Notes: Yaxel Lendeborg, Solo Ball Good To Go Injury report: Apart from LJ Cason, Michigan's guard who's missed the last month after tearing his ACL, it's a clean bill of health for both teams. There was a concern about Wolverines forward Yaxel Lendeborg, who injured his left knee on Saturday, but he is good to go. UConn wing Solo Ball also sustained an injury on Saturday, but will be available. Huskies' guard Silas Demary Jr. has been managing lower body injuries since the NCAA Tournament started, but will be available, too. Apr 06, 2026 - 7:50p ET Preview: Which Team Will Come Out on Top? Michigan punched its ticket to the championship after dominating fellow No. 1 seed Arizona by 18 points in the Final Four on Saturday evening, while UConn advanced after taking down No. 3 seed Illinois by nine points.The Wolverines have lost four consecutive championship games since beating Seton Hall in overtime in 1989 for their only national title. The Huskies won back-to-back titles in 2023 (vs. San Diego State) and 2024 (vs. Purdue). Live Coverage for this began on Apr 06, 2026 - 11:53p ET
